podcast.body: Editors are among a partial list of artists and bands who have publicly stated that they have been influenced by Joy Division in some way. podcast.title: Part of 2000s Post-Punk Revival
podcast.body: Editors emerged as part of the new generation of bands in the 2000s Post-Punk revival, demonstrating Joy Division's enduring influence. "Luego en el 2000 tuvimos ese nuevo rival del Post Punk en el que salían, pues, blockparti en el que salían los editoros, en el que salían todas estas bandas de la nueva generación del rival del Post Punk."

xref.title: Alex Kapranos's Food Writing
xref.body: Alex Kapranos began writing about food for The Guardian after an editor approached him. Despite initial skepticism about his qualifications as a musician, his past experience as a chef and the opportunity to travel globally, trying unusual foods like deep-fried locusts and bulls' testicles, provided a unique perspective. He appreciated the "naivety" his lack of a food critic's vocabulary brought to his writing. "The idea was my idea, I've got to be totally honest about that, it was one of the editors at the Guardian, approached me and said, what do you want to write about food and my immediate reaction was like, well of course I can't write about food, I'm a guy in a band, I don't know anything about it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Franz Ferdinand: In Their Own Words

xref.title: New York Dolls Fan Club Founder
xref.body: As a child, Stephen Patrick Morrissey, the singer for The Smiths, was a fervent fan of the original New York Dolls, writing letters to British music magazines to laud them and founding their British fan club. "In fact, when Morrissey was a kid, he used to write letters to the editors of various British music magazines praising the glories of the original New York dolls. He was even the founder of their British fan club."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 3

xref.title: Renaissance Image and Family Background
xref.body: Florence Welch is often described as looking as if she "stepped out of a Renaissance painting." This artistic image may be influenced by her mother, who is a professor of Renaissance studies at King's College London. Her extensive family tree also includes actors, directors, advertising executives, newspaper editors, and writers. "I've often described Florence Welch of Florence in the machine as someone who looks like they've stepped out of a Renaissance painting. Maybe it's because her mother is a professor of Renaissance studies at King's College London."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century
